clue.text: Part of the UK was invaded by the French

indicators.note: a place invaded by a force has that force inside its borders, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A history note about a French invasion of part of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: The French article sits between the second and third letters of 'was'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wales is one of the four constituent countries making up the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Offender harassed dog owner on end of pier

indicators.note: something harassed is pushed about and disturbed, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: end of asks for only the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the last letter of pier

explanation.surface: Someone at the seaside is charged with pestering a dog walker on a pier.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer is a person who commits an offence, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Tell principal of Loughborough College

indicators.note: the principal or head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of Loughborough
Eton College, the famous English public school

explanation.surface: An instruction to inform the head of a college in Loughborough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Principal' looks like a college head in the surface, but it selects a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To let on is an idiom meaning to reveal or tell a secret.

clue.text: Sleeveless shirt — team's leader is after one

parts.note: single means one

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

parts.note: the first letter of team

explanation.surface: A sports kit note: the captain wants a sleeveless top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is after' places the team's first letter behind the word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a vest-like garment without sleeves, worn by athletes.

clue.text: Purchase, on the phone before work, a derivative

indicators.note: over the phone a word is only heard, so the spelling may be a different word of the same sound

parts.note: buy means purchase, and sounds the same as the preposition
a product is a piece of work produced

explanation.surface: A telephone order placed before starting work, for some derived item.
explanation.definitionFit: A by-product is something produced incidentally from another process, so it is derived from it.

clue.text: Literary people blog Rob Roy, sum up novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A book blogger is told to review and summarise Scott's novel Rob Roy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' fits Rob Roy, Walter Scott's book, but here it means new and reshapes the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bloomsbury Group was a circle of English writers and artists including Virginia Woolf and E. M. Forster.

clue.text: Act firmly to gain momentum

definitions.meaning: second meaning: press the accelerator to speed up

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one instruction about building speed; the phrase has a figurative and a driving sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means taking a firm stand, and literally pressing the car's accelerator pedal to go faster.

clue.text: More than a couple of pounds altogether

parts.note: over means more than
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for pound (librae), so two of them

explanation.surface: Someone totals up a bill that comes to slightly over two pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Overall and altogether are synonyms meaning taking everything into account.

clue.text: Constellation seen from Mars in our galaxy?

indicators.note: a galaxy is a vast scattering of stars, suggesting these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An astronomer wonders which star pattern would be visible from Mars.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the unusual anagram signal; the surface is about stargazing, which makes 'galaxy' look like scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursa Minor, the Little Bear, is the northern constellation containing the Pole Star.

clue.text: Row about lodge's first doorkeeper

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word wraps round what follows

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

indicators.note: first asks for just the opening letter of the preceding word

parts.note: the first letter of lodge

explanation.surface: A dispute over who first guarded the door of a lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: The lodge in the surface is apt: a tiler is the officer who guards the door of a Freemasons' lodge.
explanation.definitionFit: In Freemasonry the tiler (or tyler) keeps the outer door of the lodge during meetings.

clue.text: Thorough? Off-target twice, apparently

parts.note: a shot off target is out
twice means the same word again, joined on with 'and'

explanation.surface: A shooter misses twice and wonders if the analysis was thorough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' admits the playful reading: out, and out again.
explanation.definitionFit: Out-and-out means complete or utter in every way, so thorough as an intensifying adjective.

clue.text: Treacherous type losing wife's support

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter is dropped from the word before

parts.note: a weasel is a sly, treacherous person
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A double-crosser loses the support of his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: W for wife is a standard abbreviation; it is removed from the front of the animal word.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand that supports a painter's canvas or a display board.

clue.text: Fragment Marlene forced out of wealthy landowner, perhaps

indicators.note: letters that are forced are pushed out of their natural order into a new one

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Marlene is driven out of a rich estate owner's property in pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentleman farmer owns farmland as a man of means rather than working it for a living, so a wealthy landowner is an example.

clue.text: Storming start

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an assault or attack

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it looks like a fast beginning; 'Storming' is a noun here for an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Onset means both an attack, especially a military one, and the beginning of something unpleasant.

clue.text: Able to endure stormy weather was theory, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters fall out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boat's design was meant to survive storms, but only in theory.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaworthy vessel is fit to go to sea and withstand rough conditions.

clue.text: Tennis player, contemptible on passenger ship?

parts.note: base means low and contemptible
an ocean liner carries passengers

explanation.surface: A despicable tennis player on a cruise ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the tennis player is a description, not literally on a liner.
explanation.definitionFit: A baseliner is a tennis player who stays near the back line and plays from there.

clue.text: Tries during proper practice session

indicators.note: during means within, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: real means proper or genuine
a judge hears or tries a case

explanation.surface: Rugby players score tries during a real training session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' suggests rugby or attempts, but it is the legal sense of a court hearing a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice performance before the real event.

clue.text: Hope film director's put in new oratorio

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so a letter is inserted
new signals the following word is made over into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for director

explanation.surface: A film director hopes to place a new oratorio in the score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hope' is not a wish but Bob Hope, the comedian who starred in the 'Road to' films with Bing Crosby.
explanation.definitionFit: Road to Rio (1947) is one of the Road comedy films starring Bob Hope and Bing Crosby.

clue.text: Incredible bar in European capital

parts.note: a tall story is an incredible one
an inn is a place with a bar

explanation.surface: A wonderful bar found in one of Europe's capital cities.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallinn is the capital city of Estonia.

clue.text: Hare off across middle of neutral ground

indicators.note: across means spanning over, so one part straddles the other
off means gone wrong or out of place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: middle of keeps only the central letter of the word

parts.note: the middle letter of the seven-letter neutral

explanation.surface: A hare runs off across a no-man's-land between two sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neutral ground' looks like one phrase; only 'ground' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is a synonym for ground or soil.

clue.text: Ecstasy obtained by tearaway, as a boost to self-esteem?

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
got means obtained
a rip is a reckless rascal; 'by' places it next to the rest

explanation.surface: A young tearaway takes ecstasy to feel better about himself.
explanation.walkthrough: A rip, short for rapscallion, is an old word for a wild young person.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an activity done mainly to make oneself feel important, flattering one's self-regard.

clue.text: Work for a pianist after the day job?

definitions.text: Work for a pianist after the day job?

parts.note: surface reading: a musician's evening job; setter's reading: a composition for piano
surface reading: a second job; setter's reading: the moonlighting idea, working at night after a day job

explanation.walkthrough: To moonlight is to take a second job at night, so the question mark turns Beethoven's famous piano piece into an evening shift.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Piano Sonata No. 14 is popularly known by this nickname, making it a work for pianists.

clue.text: Second suitable upturned design

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: in a down clue upturned means the word is turned upside down, reading from bottom to top

parts.note: fit means suitable

explanation.surface: A design is rejected and then accepted on second inspection when turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a recurring design or pattern element.

clue.text: Boy losing book causes alarm

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter is dropped from the name before

parts.note: a boy's name
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A child loses his book and panics.
explanation.definitionFit: An alert is a warning signal, the same as an alarm.

clue.text: Expresses mild disapproval in front of one Bantu tribe member

parts.note: to tut is to click the tongue in mild disapproval
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone tuts at a member of an African people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are a Bantu-speaking people of Rwanda and Burundi, so a Tutsi is one member.

clue.text: Lourdes so relaxing being free from smell

indicators.note: relaxing loosens the order of the letters so they can be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pilgrim finds Lourdes calming because the air is fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: Lourdes is the French pilgrimage town; its letters plus 'so' are reshuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Odourless means having no smell at all.

clue.text: Tiny fish in good bowl, item used by cook

parts.note: fry are young, very small fish
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good
a pan is a bowl-shaped vessel

explanation.surface: Little fish served in a nice bowl, something a chef uses.
explanation.definitionFit: A frying pan is a shallow pan that a cook uses for frying food.

clue.text: Floral feature has tulip's head in centre of ring

indicators.note: placed in the centre of something means set inside it

parts.note: a peal is a ring of bells

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of tulip

explanation.surface: A floral display has a tulip at the centre of a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A petal is one of the coloured parts of a flower, a feature of any bloom.
